title: Design Optimization of Caesium Contents for Mixed Cation MA1-xCsxPbI3 Based Efficient Perovskite Solar Cell
content: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have already been reported as a promising alternative to traditional energy sources due to their excellent power-conversion efficiency, affordability, and versatility, which is particularly relevant considering the growing worldwide demand for energy and in-creasing scarcity of natural resources. However, stability concerns under environmental stresses hinder its economic feasibility. Through the addition of caesium (Cs), this study investigates how to optimize perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on methylammonium lead-iodide (MAPbI3) by cre-ating mixed-cation compositions of MA1-xCsxPbI3 (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) for devices A to E re-spectively. The impact of caesium content on the following factors such as open-circuit voltage (Voc), short-circuit current density (Jsc), fill-factor (FF), and as well as power-conversion efficiency (PCE) was investigated in five different devices architectures using simulation software. The ar-chitecture included ITO/ TiO2/ MA1-xCsxPbI3 / Spiro-OMeTAD/Au. Due to enhanced crystal stabil-ity and diminished defect density, the device with x = 0.5 (MA0.5Cs0.5PbI3) attains a maximum power conversion efficiency of 18.53%, with a Voc of 0.9238 V, Jsc of 24.22 mA/cm², and a fill-factor of 82.81%. The optimal doping density of TiO2 at approximately 1020 cm-3, the optimal thicknesses of the electron -transport layer (TiO2, 10-30 nm), the hole-transport layer (Spiro-OMeTAD, about 150 nm), and the perovskite absorber (75 nm) were identified to maximize effi-ciency. Phase stability and moisture resistance are both enhanced by Cs addition, but PCE is re-duced at high concentrations (x  > 0.5) because of phase instability and trap states. The results show that mixed-cation perovskite solar cells can be a great commercially viable option because they strike a good balance between efficiency and stability.
